# Lessons — fin-attribute-extraction (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B)

Workload: prefill-dominated structured extraction (ISL ~1.6K/p90 4.7K, OSL ~22), tight 1s/2s E2E SLO @ 70 RPS peak. Benchmarked g7e (sm_120), H200 (sm_90), B200 (sm_100), all vLLM 0.22.1 FP8 TP1. Full 3-way report: `docs/reports/fin-attribute-extraction-g7e-20260615.html`.

## Headline outcome
Serve as independent FP8 **TP1 replicas behind a router** — not TP2, not disaggregated. Model is 3B-active MoE (~32 GB FP8) fitting one GPU with ~113× KV headroom. For 70 RPS: ~4 H200 / ~4 B200 / ~6 g7e GPUs. Per-replica SLO-safe knee: g7e ~12, H200 ~20, B200 ~22 RPS. H200 cheapest per unit of capacity ($0.096/sustained-RPS-hr).

---

## Cross-cutting (candidates for steering)

### L1 — vLLM full CUDA-graph capture is sm-arch-specific; it's the ~2× per-replica differentiator
Full-decode CUDA-graph capture (`Capturing CUDA graphs (decode, FULL)`) **SUCCEEDS on H200 (sm_90) and B200 (sm_100), CRASHES on g7e (sm_120)** with `AssertionError: 1 != <ISL>` for this hybrid Gated-DeltaNet MoE on vLLM 0.22.1. This — not raw FLOPs/bandwidth — is why g7e is launch-bound (SM ~43%, knee ~12 RPS) while the datacenter parts are compute-bound (SM ~99-100%, knee ~20-22 RPS). The MoE backend was **TRITON on all three** (identical kernel path), so the kernel is not the differentiator. Implication: a launch-bound knee on one GPU is not proof a bigger GPU won't help — re-test graph-capture per arch before concluding hardware is the limit.

### L2 — GPU spot nodegroups on qwen3-next-bench cluster launch WITHOUT the node SG
Both the B200 and H200 spot nodegroups launched with only the cluster SG (`sg-0abb08cf4d13be131`), missing the node SG (`sg-0bf5ad07fc6c29df1`). Result: ALL pod networking silently broken (cross-node pod-to-pod, FSx, in-cluster DNS) — manifests as connection timeouts / DNS failures inside pods, not an obvious SG error. Fix: attach the node SG to the instance's primary ENI after launch. This was the root cause of a multi-hour failure cascade on the first (B200) encounter.

### L3 — bake `nvidia.com/gpu.present=true` into nodegroup `--labels`
The NVIDIA device plugin daemonset has nodeSelector `nvidia.com/gpu.present=true`. A nodegroup created without that label reports 0 allocatable GPUs until labeled. The H200 nodegroup baked it into `--labels` and the device plugin attached automatically; an ad-hoc B200 node needed a manual `kubectl label`. Always set it in the nodegroup config.

### L4 — GPU nodes have no internet egress + FSx-Lustre CSI fails → use the FSx-HTTP fetch pattern
GPU nodes on this cluster have no internet egress (can't reach HF or apt repos) and the FSx-Lustre CSI mount fails on the GPU AMIs (`mount.lustre: Can't parse NID`). Pattern that works: stage weights to FSx from a CPU node (which has egress + working CSI), serve them over HTTP from a CPU-node pod (`python3 -m http.server`), and fetch to the GPU node's emptyDir over the pod network with a pure-Python downloader (no apt/curl/egress needed). Reference ClusterIP via service IP if in-cluster DNS is flaky.

### L5 — mnbt ≥ ISL for prefill-dominated, launch-bound workloads (do not chunk below ISL)
`--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` (≥ the ~2500-token ISL) gave ~20% more SLO-safe capacity than default and far more than mnbt=2048/4096. Sizing mnbt *below* the ISL forces prefill chunking → more scheduler iterations → more kernel launches, which is the scarce resource when launch-bound. This is the OPPOSITE of the spec's hypothesis (which suggested chunking down to pack short-output requests). Same lesson as Nemotron-3-Super.

### L6 — MoE tile tuning is a no-op for a launch-bound knee, even when the Triton path loads the config
On g7e the FP8 MoE path is Triton and warned "default MoE config — sub-optimal". We generated the missing tile config (`E=256,N=512,fp8_w8a8`), confirmed vLLM loaded it, and measured zero improvement. The launch-bound bound is the *number* of kernel launches, not per-GEMM tile efficiency — tile tuning can't reduce dispatch count. (Differs from Nemotron/B200 where tuning was inert because the kernel was FlashInfer and never read the JSON.) Don't tune MoE tiles to fix a launch-bound knee.

### L7 — measure DCGM bottleneck class with continuous in-pod `nvidia-smi dmon`, not point-sampled DCGM PROF
DCGM-exporter PROF fields (SM_ACTIVE, etc.) point-sampled over the pod network missed the bursty load peaks (read 0.15 SM during gaps). Continuous in-pod `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` gave the reliable steady-state read (SM 100%, mem 47% at the H200 knee). Also: Prometheus in this cluster is NOT scraping the DCGM exporter (no ServiceMonitor) — scrape the exporter pod directly on :9400 if you need the rich fields.

## Model-specific (mdc feedback for qwen3.6-35b)

### M1 — arch registers as `qwen3_5_moe` (Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration)
Same family as Qwen3.5; vLLM 0.22.1 serves it. Hybrid Gated-DeltaNet (linear attn, 3 of every 4 layers) + full-attention MoE, 256 experts (8 routed), moe_intermediate_size=512, 40 layers, ~72 GB bf16 / ~32 GB FP8. Multimodal (vision encoder present, unused for text extraction).

### M2 — disable thinking per-request or it blows the SLO
`chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False}` → output is the bare value (~2 tokens, no `<think>`). Default-on thinking emits ~64 tokens of deliberation that blows the 1s SLO. A regression that re-enables it is the single biggest deployment risk for this workload.

### M3 — vision-encoder CUTLASS ICE on datacenter GPUs → serve text-only
On both H200 (sm_90) and B200 (sm_100), vLLM 0.22.1 hits a CUTLASS-DSL compile crash (`vit_flash_attn_wrapper` → `cute.compile` → ICE) during dummy-run profiling of the vision encoder, right after weight load. Serve text-only with `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}'` to skip ViT profiling. g7e dodged it via a different ViT attention path.

### M4 — `max_num_seqs` default 1024 > Mamba cache blocks → cap at 256
Default max_num_seqs (1024) exceeds available Mamba cache blocks (754) for the hybrid layers → CUDA-graph capture refuses to start. Set `--max-num-seqs 256` (the workload's target concurrency is 50 anyway).

### M5 — FP8 + data-parallel is broken on vLLM 0.22.1 for this hybrid GDN MoE
`--data-parallel-size 2` with FP8 dies on first request with `AssertionError: 1 != <ISL>` in the all-reduce/sequence-parallel path. bf16 DP=2 worked. Workaround: run independent single-GPU TP1 replicas behind a router (no DP coordinator).

### M6 — first-batch JIT is brutal; always warm up before measuring
fused_moe_kernel + GDN/causal-conv1d kernels JIT-compile on first unseen shape → 32 s cold TTFT, then ~93 ms warm. A cold server looks wedged; always run a warmup pass before benchmarking.

### M7 — no official FP8; online `--quantization fp8` (per-tensor) works
No official FP8 checkpoint. vLLM online `--quantization fp8` (per-tensor dynamic) fits ~32 GB and serves; quality vs a real extraction corpus is unverified. FP8 ≈ 2× the SLO-safe per-replica rate of bf16 on g7e (admission-ceiling bound, not bandwidth).

### M8 — FP8 MoE TP-divisibility: TP1/2/4 OK, TP8 forbidden
moe_intermediate_size 512 / TP % 128 == 0 → TP1/2/4 valid, TP8 (512/8=64) forbidden. Moot in practice — the model fits TP1 with huge headroom; use TP1 replicas.

- us-east-2 EKS nodegroup subnets: `subnet-0173f4f14b36994cd` (2b) lacks public-IP auto-assign and failed nodegroup create; `subnet-03d03f1fb8d62d6a5` (2b, NAT-routed) works — used by the B200 nodegroup too.
- p5en spot is the H200 instance in this region; p5e cheaper if available. Networking variant (p5en vs p5e) irrelevant here — TP1, no collective.
